details.description: DeepSeek-R1 is DeepSeek AI's first-generation reasoning model, released January 2025 and documented in an accompanying arXiv paper (2501.12948) as achieving performance comparable to OpenAI's o1 on math, code and reasoning tasks. It is a 671-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 37 billion active parameters, built from a DeepSeek-V3-Base checkpoint and trained with large-scale reinforcement learning to produce extended chain-of-thought reasoning before its final answer, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository. DeepSeek originally served R1 on its own platform under the deepseek-reasoner model name, but DeepSeek's changelog shows that alias was reassigned away from R1 to DeepSeek-V3.1 as early as August 2025, then to several later V3.x releases; DeepSeek's current API pricing page lists only deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro, with deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner no longer listed at all following their announced 2026-07-24 discontinuation. The open-weight model remains downloadable from DeepSeek directly and, per Bud's catalog, is still served through third-party hosts such as Fireworks AI and Hyperbolic.
advantages: Scores 79.8% on AIME 2024 (pass@1), close to OpenAI o1's 79.2%, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Scores 97.3% on MATH-500 (pass@1), per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Scores 71.5% on GPQA Diamond, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Released under the MIT License, permitting commercial use and distillation into smaller models, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
DeepSeek has released six smaller distilled variants (1.5B-70B, Qwen- and Llama-based) trained on DeepSeek-R1 outputs, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
disadvantages: DeepSeek's current API documentation no longer lists standalone R1 among its active models; the deepseek-reasoner alias that served R1 was reassigned to DeepSeek-V3.1 in August 2025 (a year before any V4 model existed), and the alias itself was discontinued by 2026-07-24 alongside deepseek-chat.
Superseded on DeepSeek's own reasoning line by the May 2025 DeepSeek-R1-0528 update, which DeepSeek reports scores substantially higher on the same benchmarks.
DeepSeek's usage guidance for R1 recommends against system prompts and a temperature of 0.5-0.7.
Text only; no image or audio input or output, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
use_cases: General reasoning tasks requiring an explicit chain-of-thought before a final answer.

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens (32768/65536/128000) and max_output_tokens (8192/20480/32768) vary by provider (DeepSeek's own API, Fireworks, Hyperbolic) and are kept as given; DeepSeek's GitHub repository documents a 128,000-token native context, matching the catalog's highest max_input value, while Fireworks' own R1 page separately lists a larger 163,840-token window for its speed-optimized deployment -- not reconciled against catalog's numbers. Correction: DeepSeek's changelog shows the deepseek-reasoner alias served R1 (from 2025-01-20), then R1-0528 (from 2025-05-28), then was reassigned to DeepSeek-V3.1 on 2025-08-21 -- well before any V4 model existed -- and continued through V3.1-Terminus, V3.2-Exp, V3.2 and finally V4-Flash (2026-04-24). That same 2026-04-24 entry separately announced deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner would be discontinued by 2026-07-24; as of this research neither name appears on DeepSeek's current pricing page, which lists only deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro. Fireworks' own R1 page showed no deprecation marking as of this research, and Bud's catalog still lists deepseek, fireworks_ai-embedding-models and hyperbolicai as providers.
